headline: BIS issued sweeping new export controls covering advanced computing chips and chipmaking equipment bound for China
Analysts and commentators called the October 2022 controls a landmark shift in US-China tech relations, with one describing it as close to an act of economic war
Nvidia and peer chipmakers traded lower as reports emerged the US planned to further tighten the chip export restrictions announced in October
AMD shares fell alongside Nvidia as the new China export restrictions rattled the broader semiconductor sector
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell roughly 8% following the October 2022 export control announcement, based on CSIS analysis of the sector-wide reaction
BIS released updated interim final rules on October 17, 2023, closing loopholes in the 2022 controls and expanding country coverage
Then-Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo said the update was meant to close loopholes and signaled the rules would likely be revised annually
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell roughly 3% following the October 2023 update, a smaller move than the 2022 announcement, per CSIS analysis
ASML shares dipped about 1.3% after the Dutch government partially revoked an export licence for two of its lithography machine models bound for China
China's foreign ministry criticized the Dutch licence revocation and urged the Netherlands to protect bilateral supply chain stability
BIS issued new December 2024 rules placing country-wide restrictions on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) exports to China for the first time
Analysts noted the new HBM restrictions could indirectly benefit Nvidia by hurting Chinese AI chip competitors reliant on the same memory technology
The December 2024 rules also expanded restrictions on semiconductor manufacturing equipment and added new entities to the BIS Entity List
